studyGuide.sectionTitle: Chapter keywords: explain, distinguish and exemplify

elements.text: These are original plain-language explanations, not quotations from the official glossary. For each term, give a new example and explain its difference from a neighboring term. Use the official glossary with the CTFL syllabus context for authoritative wording.

rows: anomaly
An observation that differs from expectations and needs investigation before classification.
dynamic testing
Evaluate software by executing it and observing results.
formal review
A review conducted with a defined process, responsibilities and recorded evidence appropriate to its formality.
informal review
An examination without a required formal process or prescribed documented output.
inspection
The most formal review type, with defined roles, a complete process and collected metrics.
review
People examine a work product to identify anomalies, improve understanding and assess quality.
static analysis
Tool-supported examination of structured artifacts without executing the test object.
static testing
Examine work products through reviews or static analysis without executing them.
technical review
Technically qualified reviewers use moderated discussion to assess a technical issue and seek decisions or consensus.
walkthrough
The author leads participants through a work product to explain it, collect questions and identify anomalies.

elements.text: Official exam weighting: 4/40 questions (10%). Work in short topic blocks; retrieve before rereading. The chapter quiz contains 16 original questions across all objectives of this chapter. Revisit high-confidence errors with Smart Review and use the full official chapter and keywords to check completeness.

elements.description: Reviews can examine requirements, designs, code, tests, contracts and other readable work products. Static analysis needs an analyzable structure or syntax. Neither requires execution of the test object.

elements.text: Worked example: Reviewing an acceptance criterion is possible before software exists; measuring running response time is dynamic.
Close the notes: Name three non-code work products suitable for static testing.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: FL-3.1.2 · Value of static testing · K2

elements.description: Static testing exposes defects directly and can find ambiguity, inconsistency, omissions and unreachable code early. It can reduce downstream cost and improve shared understanding.

elements.text: Worked example: A requirements review finds contradictory currencies before developers implement either interpretation.
Close the notes: Explain an early defect that dynamic execution might struggle to identify directly.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: FL-3.1.3 · Static and dynamic testing · K2

elements.description: Static testing examines a work product without executing it; dynamic testing executes software and observes behavior. They find overlapping but different defect types and complement one another.

elements.text: Worked example: A review spots a missing rule; an execution test exposes a timeout under load.
Close the notes: Choose the technique based on the evidence needed, not on whether a tool is used.

elements.description: Frequent feedback helps correct misunderstandings early, clarifies requirements and reduces the cost of building the wrong product.

elements.text: Worked example: A customer reviews a small draft workflow and corrects a mistaken assumption before implementation.
Close the notes: Recall how smaller, earlier feedback cycles reduce wasted work.

elements.description: Plan the review; initiate it with access and instructions; review individually; communicate and analyze anomalies; fix and report. An anomaly is investigated before it is classified as a defect.

elements.text: Worked example: Reviewers first record observations independently, then discuss which require changes, before the author fixes them.
Close the notes: Distinguish individual review from communication and analysis.

elements.description: The manager allocates support and resources; the author creates and fixes the work product; the moderator facilitates; the scribe records; reviewers examine; the review leader organizes and takes overall responsibility.

elements.text: Worked example: A moderator keeps a review constructive while the scribe records decisions and anomalies.
Close the notes: Match facilitation, recording and overall organization to roles.

elements.description: Informal reviews need no defined formal process; walkthroughs are author-led; technical reviews use qualified reviewers and a moderator; inspections use the most formal process and collect metrics. In inspections the author cannot be review leader or scribe.

elements.text: Worked example: A formal inspection checks entry and exit conditions and records metrics; an author-led teaching session is a walkthrough.
Close the notes: Choose a review type from its defining process characteristics.

elements.description: Use clear objectives, small work products, preparation time, trained participants, management support and a constructive culture. Review work products rather than using defects to appraise people.

elements.text: Worked example: A short prepared review with an explicit objective encourages useful findings; a blame meeting suppresses them.
Close the notes: Recall three conditions that make reviews more effective.
Attempt these after studying the chapter, without looking at the keyword table. Explain each answer in your own words, then open the solution.

elements.title: Static versus dynamic testing
elements.prompt: Test 1: reviewers read a user story and find a contradictory acceptance criterion. Test 2: a test run of the built feature shows a wrong total. Which is static testing, and what does each find?
elements.solution: Test 1 is static testing: nothing is executed, and the review finds the defect directly. Test 2 is dynamic testing: execution causes a failure, which must then be analysed to locate the defect.

elements.title: Choose the review type
elements.prompt: (1) The author leads a session to explain a design to new team members and gather ideas. (2) Technically qualified reviewers, led by a moderator, must decide between two architecture options. (3) A review with defined roles, collected metrics and an author who cannot act as review leader or scribe aims to find as many anomalies as possible. Name each review type.
elements.solution: (1) Walkthrough. (2) Technical review. (3) Inspection, the most formal type. An informal review follows no defined process and requires no formal documented output.

elements.title: Static analysis versus review
elements.prompt: A tool reports unreachable code and a variable used before it is assigned. Later, three colleagues read the design document and discuss its gaps. Which activity is static analysis, which is a review, and what do they have in common?
elements.solution: The tool-based check is static analysis; the colleagues reading the document perform a review. Both are static testing: neither executes the software.

elements.title: Anomaly versus defect
elements.prompt: Reviewers log 12 anomalies. After analysis, 9 are confirmed as defects, 2 are misunderstandings by the reviewers and 1 is a change request. Why are the logged items called anomalies?
elements.solution: An anomaly is a condition that deviates from expectation. In the review process, each logged anomaly is then evaluated and given a status and action: a defect, not a defect, or a different action such as a change request.

examPitfalls.title: FL-3.1.1 · Static test objects
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Only source code can be a static test object.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Reviews can examine requirements, designs, code, tests, contracts and other readable work products. Static analysis needs an analyzable structure or syntax. Neither requires execution of the test object. Self-check: Name three non-code work products suitable for static testing.

examPitfalls.title: FL-3.1.2 · Value of static testing
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Reviews cannot find useful defects until executable software is available.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Static testing exposes defects directly and can find ambiguity, inconsistency, omissions and unreachable code early. It can reduce downstream cost and improve shared understanding. Self-check: Explain an early defect that dynamic execution might struggle to identify directly.

examPitfalls.title: FL-3.1.3 · Static and dynamic testing
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Tool-assisted testing is automatically dynamic, while manual testing is automatically static.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Static testing examines a work product without executing it; dynamic testing executes software and observes behavior. They find overlapping but different defect types and complement one another. Self-check: Choose the technique based on the evidence needed, not on whether a tool is used.

examPitfalls.title: FL-3.2.1 · Early stakeholder feedback
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Stakeholder feedback should be postponed until final acceptance to avoid changing drafts.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Frequent feedback helps correct misunderstandings early, clarifies requirements and reduces the cost of building the wrong product. Self-check: Recall how smaller, earlier feedback cycles reduce wasted work.

examPitfalls.title: FL-3.2.2 · Review process
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Every recorded review anomaly is automatically a confirmed defect requiring the proposed fix.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Plan the review; initiate it with access and instructions; review individually; communicate and analyze anomalies; fix and report. An anomaly is investigated before it is classified as a defect. Self-check: Distinguish individual review from communication and analysis.

examPitfalls.title: FL-3.2.3 · Review roles
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The moderator, scribe and review leader have identical responsibilities.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The manager allocates support and resources; the author creates and fixes the work product; the moderator facilitates; the scribe records; reviewers examine; the review leader organizes and takes overall responsibility. Self-check: Match facilitation, recording and overall organization to roles.

examPitfalls.title: FL-3.2.4 · Review types
examPitfalls.trapDescription: An inspection is just an author-led walkthrough with a more formal name.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Informal reviews need no defined formal process; walkthroughs are author-led; technical reviews use qualified reviewers and a moderator; inspections use the most formal process and collect metrics. In inspections the author cannot be review leader or scribe. Self-check: Choose a review type from its defining process characteristics.

examPitfalls.title: FL-3.2.5 · Review success
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Reviews should primarily evaluate the performance of individual authors.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use clear objectives, small work products, preparation time, trained participants, management support and a constructive culture. Review work products rather than using defects to appraise people. Self-check: Recall three conditions that make reviews more effective.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which work product can be reviewed before executable software exists?

options.text: A user story with acceptance criteria

practiceQuiz.rationale: A readable story can be examined statically. The other evidence requires observing execution.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which is a suitable target for static analysis with an appropriate analyzer?

options.text: The observed latency of a live request
The behavior of a running recovery process

practiceQuiz.rationale: Static analysis evaluates structured artifacts without running them. The other targets are runtime behavior.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why can static testing lower lifecycle costs?

options.text: It can reveal misunderstandings before they spread into later artifacts
It guarantees that no dynamic tests will fail

practiceQuiz.rationale: Early correction can avoid downstream rework. Static tests neither guarantee execution results nor directly measure production behavior or replace collaboration.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which finding particularly illustrates the value of a requirements review?

options.text: Two rules prescribe conflicting cancellation deadlines
The server slows under 5,000 concurrent sessions
A process leaks memory during repeated requests
A network link fails under load

practiceQuiz.rationale: Conflicting written rules are directly visible statically. The other findings depend on execution and operational conditions.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tool identifies unreachable code without running the program. What is this?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Tool use does not make a test dynamic. No program execution occurred; acceptance and load execution require running behavior.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why combine reviews with execution tests?

options.text: They expose different kinds of evidence and defects
Both techniques guarantee complete defect detection
Reviews are useful only after execution fails

practiceQuiz.rationale: They complement one another. Neither guarantees completeness; reviews can start early and dynamic tests can evaluate specified outputs.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which is a benefit of showing a small draft to users early?

options.text: Misunderstandings can be corrected before more work depends on them
The users become solely responsible for defects

practiceQuiz.rationale: Early feedback reduces wasted work and uncertainty without eliminating testing, transferring all responsibility or removing all risk.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: When should stakeholder feedback first be sought on a draft workflow?

options.text: When a useful reviewable draft is available
Only at the formal release meeting
After every technical test has passed

practiceQuiz.rationale: Early reviewable increments enable timely correction. Delaying feedback until late gates loses that benefit.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Reviewers independently note anomalies before a review discussion. Which activity is this?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Individual review examines the work product. Discussion comes afterward; fixing/reporting follows analysis, and release authorization is outside this activity.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why analyze recorded review anomalies before requiring changes?

options.text: Discussion replaces the need to record decisions
Every reviewer observation must be implemented unchanged
An anomaly may be a misunderstanding rather than a confirmed defect

practiceQuiz.rationale: Investigation classifies observations. Blind acceptance, reliability guarantees and unrecorded decisions do not follow from a review.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which review role facilitates an effective meeting?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The moderator facilitates. The scribe records; the author creates and corrects the product; configuration administration is a different responsibility.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Who records review decisions and consolidates observations?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Recording review information is the scribe's responsibility. The other roles are not defined by that duty.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An author leads colleagues through a work product to teach and collect feedback. Which review type fits?
practiceQuiz.rationale: An author-led examination is a walkthrough. Inspection has different formal role restrictions; the other activities are not this review type.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which feature distinguishes an inspection from an informal review?

options.text: The author must serve as scribe
No need to prepare before the meeting
A formal process with recorded metrics and defined roles
Mandatory execution of the reviewed program

practiceQuiz.rationale: Inspections use a formal process and metrics. Execution is unnecessary, preparation matters and the author cannot act as inspection scribe.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

options.text: Omitting role training to save meeting time
Evaluating the author's salary using anomaly counts
Clear objectives and adequate preparation time
Reviewing the largest possible artifact in one sitting

practiceQuiz.rationale: Objectives and preparation improve effectiveness. Personal appraisal, oversized reviews and untrained roles undermine it.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How should a team use findings from reviews?

options.text: Postpone fixes until operational failures appear
Rank individual authors without considering context
Improve work products and feed lessons into the process

practiceQuiz.rationale: Reviews support product and process improvement. Blame, concealment and waiting for failures lose preventive value.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.
